name: osd-aa-font
summary: Anti-aliased OSD text: Noto Sans Condensed SemiBold 14 px rendered as 2-bit (4-level) glyphs, smooth edges in every text colour; filled rounded selection bar; multiplication sign in the resolution line
status: experimental; v1 on hardware 2026-10-09: menu items showed parts of other strings; v2 on hardware: strings right, colours wrong (palette rule); v3 (palette entry = attribute & 0xFC + value) hardware-tested: correct, text slightly blurry; v4 (stems on pixel edges, selection bar, ×) on hardware: text sharper; first item's bar touched the header band, item text on the bar had a transparent background (2-bit tiles with attribute 0x61); v5 (text on the bar with attribute 0x60, 3 px gap below the header band) hardware test pending

notes: Text tiles become 2-bit glyphs (two code slots each). Logical codes L = bank << 8 | slot map to 2-bit codes: 0x009-0x01B -> 2L+0x66, 0x020-0x150 -> 2L+0x5E, 0x151-0x181 -> 2L+0x6E, 0x1C0-0x1D9 -> 2L+0x4A; vendor icons stay at 0x300-0x30F and 0x372-0x3C9; 2-bit range from 0x078 (0x101C0A). Each text attribute gets a 4-entry palette at entries 0x40-0x6F (tile attribute = its first entry; a 2-bit tile uses entries (attribute & 0xFC) + value) with [background, 1/3, 2/3, foreground] of its 1-bit colours, in the vendor palette table and reloaded after every palette load. Chinese and Japanese are not supported (their glyph set holds the second bit plane). Font: Noto Sans Condensed SemiBold (SIL Open Font License 1.1, docs/licenses/NotoSans-OFL.txt).
